stories.headline: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.title: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.summary: Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy to reject the election petition preferred by former DMK Minister K.R. Periakaruppan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) rejected an election petition filed against the victory of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy from Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district by a razor-thin margin of just one vote in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Asepolls.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the TVK MLA to reject the election petition filed by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) candidate and former Minister K.R. Periakaruppan, who contended that he lost the polls primarily because of the existence of two Legislative Assembly constituencies with the same name ‘Tirupattur’ in Tamil Nadu.
Mr. Sethupathy was declared elected on securing 83,375 votes as against 83,374 votes garnered by Mr. Periakaruppan.

However, the DMK candidate claimed a postal vote belonging to the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district had been inadvertently sent to the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district and that the wrongly transferred vote was not sent back to the right constituency.

Listing out the reasons for seeking a rejection of the election petition, senior counsel V. Raghavachari, assisted by advocates Dixita Gohil and Pranjal Agarwal, argued the election petitioner had presented a “highly implausible” scenario of a postal vote belonging to one constituency having been sent to another constituency just because of their identical names.

He contended the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, make the identity of the intended constituency extremely difficult to lose by pressing into service multiple independent identifiers, which could enable the authorities to determine the constituency to which a postal ballot belongs.

The counsel pointed out the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district was identified as constituency number 50, whereas the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district was identified as constituency number 185.
He asserted that the constituency number, and not the name, was the key identifier.

He said every voter who intends to exercise his/her franchise through the postal ballot must make an application, using Form 12, to the Returning Officer concerned and therefore, the constituency gets determined emphatically even before the issuance of a postal ballot to an elector.

Further, the postal ballots have the full address of the Returning Officer of the relevant constituency pre-printed, without the need for the voters to fill it up by hand, and the postal covers too clearly mention the constituency name, number, district, and the full address of the Returning Officer.

“This means the postal ballot is not an anonymous page, which can ordinarily be treated as belonging to a constituency which happens to receive it by accident, coincidence, or otherwise,” Mr. Raghavachari said and added that it was the election officials who transport the postal covers.
The senior counsel also argued the election petitioner had not produced any material but for an affidavit filed by Tirupattur district DMK candidate.

stories.headline: Election Commission row: Mumbai Police deny CJP permission for October 2 protest at Shivaji Park
stories.title: Election Commission row: Mumbai Police deny CJP permission for October 2 protest at Shivaji Park
stories.summary: They cite court-imposed curbs on non-sporting activities at the ground, lack of BMC permission and concerns over noise and traffic congestion
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Mumbai Police have denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to hold a protest against the Election Commission at Shivaji Park on October 2, citing court-imposed restrictions on non-sporting activities at the ground, lack of BMC permission and concerns over noise and traffic congestion.
The Shivaji Park police conveyed the decision in a September 27 letter addressed to CJP national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde.
The party had sought permission to hold the protest at Shivaji Park in Dadar from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m. on October 2.
The police primarily cited restrictions imposed by the Bombay High Court on the use of Shivaji Park for activities other than sports.
The notice referred to orders passed in a Public Interest Litigation petition of 2009, including a January 4, 2013 order concerning the use of the ground for non-sporting activities.
The High Court has previously restricted the use of Shivaji Park for non-sporting purposes, subject to specified exceptions and permissions.

The police also said the organisers had not submitted a permission letter for the use of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation-owned ground, as required under a Maharashtra government's Urban Development Department decision dated January 20, 2016.
The third ground cited was the possible impact of the proposed gathering on residents, traffic and hospitals in the vicinity.
“Since the said area is a peaceful and residential area, the possibility of noise pollution cannot be ruled out,” the police communication said.
It added that the protest could lead to “huge traffic” in and around Shivaji Park and said congestion could affect the movement of patients as several hospitals are located in the area.
Citing the High Court orders as well as the State government's 2016 decision, the police said permission for the October 2 protest at Shivaji Park and its surrounding area was being denied.
However, the police have not barred the CJP from holding a protest elsewhere in Mumbai.

stories.headline: Keran Mela 2026 concludes; highlights tourism, culture, community participation
stories.title: Keran Mela 2026 concludes; highlights tourism, culture, community participation
stories.summary: Kupwara, Sep 27: The three-week-long Keran Mela 2026 concluded successfully today, coinciding with World Tourism Day, at the frontier village of Keran in north Kashmir's Kupwara district, bringing to a close a series of sporting, cultural and public outreach activities aimed at showcasing the region's natural beauty, cultural heritage and unique border identity. Jointly organised by the District Administration Kupwara in collaboration with the Indian Army and the Tourism Department, the mela witnessed participation of local residents, youth and visitors through sporting competitions, cultural programmes and public outreach activities. Cricket, volleyball, Gatka, 200-metre race (Run for Fun), tug-of-war and athletics were among the sporting events, while traditional dances, instrumental music and artistic performances showcased the region's cultural vibrancy. Speaking on the occasion, Deputy Commissioner Kupwara, Shrikant Suse, expressed gratitude to the Indian Army for its continued partnership and appreciated the people of Keran for their enthusiastic participation in making the mela a success. He said that Keran possesses immense potential for sustainable tourism and emphasised the need to preserve its pristine environment, rich cultural heritage and unique border identity. He noted that such initiatives complement the objectives of the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP), under which border villages like Keran are being developed with improved infrastructure, connectivity and tourism potential, thereby strengthening both the economic and strategic resilience of frontier areas. He said the administration would continue to support initiatives aimed at promoting responsible tourism, creating livelihood opportunities for local youth and strengthening civil-army-community engagement. Highlighting the importance of environmental protection, he said the "Green Keran, Clean Keran" campaign would be further strengthened, with a dedicated SUP Check Point to be established shortly at the entry point to Keran to discourage visitors from carrying single-use plastic into the area, promote responsible tourist behaviour and ensure proper collection and disposal of waste. Addressing the gathering, Major General Rakesh Nair highlighted the importance of organising such events in far-flung areas, noting that they help preserve cultural traditions while taking government services and welfare schemes closer to the people. The mela also featured stalls for medical screening, career counselling, tourism guidance and drug de-addiction awareness, besides stalls showcasing local handicrafts and organic agricultural produce. Registered homestays and local eateries further provided visitors an opportunity to experience local hospitality, while the "Green Keran, Clean Keran" campaign ensured that the celebrations remained environmentally responsible and sustainable. The concluding ceremony also witnessed the distribution of prizes among participants and presentation of certificates of appreciation in recognition of contributions towards the successful conduct of the event. The conclusion of Keran Mela 2026 marked the culmination of a three-week-long celebration that brought together sports, culture, tourism and public services, further highlighting Keran's potential as a border tourism destination and its growing opportunities for local economic activity. Senior officers from the District Administration, Police and Indian Army, along with a large public gathering, were present on the occasion, marking the event a resounding success.

stories.headline: Believe Bengal Speaker aware of deadline on TMC rebels disqualification: SC
stories.title: Believe Bengal Speaker aware of deadline on TMC rebels disqualification: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday said it has every reason to believe that the West Bengal Assembly speaker is "fully cognisant" of the apex court's order fixing a three-month time frame to decide the disqualification petition against 10 rebel TMC MLAs. The observations came from a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana during the hearing of a plea filed by Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction MLA Sohandeb Chattopadhyay. In his petition, Chattopadhyay sought direction to the speaker to expeditiously decide the disqualification petition filed against the rebel MLAs. "We have every reason to believe that the speaker is fully cognisant of the decision of this court and he will make an endeavour to take an appropriate decision within the time-frame fixed," the bench said while disposing of the plea. The top court noted that in this case, the three-month period would expire on October 10. Chattopadhyay had earlier approached Speaker Rathin Bose

stories.headline: Blueleaf Energy Acquires 40 MW Operating Wind Asset in Karnataka
stories.title: Blueleaf Energy Acquires 40 MW Operating Wind Asset in Karnataka
stories.summary: Pan-Asian renewable energy platform Blueleaf Energy has acquired a 40 MW operating wind power asset in Karnataka’s Belagavi district. The operational wind farm has eight years of clean energy generation experience and complements Blueleaf Energy’s existing 1.5 GW greenfield portfolio across India. It includes projects under construction and in operation. The company secured its legal, finance, and tax structuring advice from Talwar Thakore & Associates (TT&A) and EY. “This acquisition marks an important milestone as our first operating asset purchase in India. Building upon our established success in greenfield development, we are now pursuing targeted M&A to accelerate our growth and scale our presence while maintaining a strong focus on delivering long-term value for India’s clean energy transition,” said Pratyush Thakur, Country Head, India, Blueleaf Energy. Blueleaf Energy’s Previous Projects in India Previously, Blueleaf Energy, commissioned its 300 MWp Pachora Hybrid Power Project in Madhya Pradesh. The project is jointly owned by Blueleaf Energy and Jakson Green through its parent company, Jakson Limited. The utility-scale wind and solar project has an estimated value of approximately ₹1,900 crore. The merchant project is expected to generate nearly 600 million units (MU) of clean electricity annually, which will be sold on the Indian power market. Blueleaf Energy has also established a presence in Rajasthan through its partnership with Jakson Green, with 280 MWp and 560 MWp ground-mounted solar plants in Bikaner forming part of the 1 GWp Rajasthan Solar Portfolio. The partners recently achieved financial close for the portfolio with Axis Bank, marking the completion of funding for the entirety of the portfolio.

stories.headline: Amid concerns over Russia sanctions law, Foreign Secretary meets U.S. delegation
stories.title: Amid concerns over Russia sanctions law, Foreign Secretary meets U.S. delegation
stories.summary: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri raised the new law with the delegation, most of whom voted in favour of sanctions targeting India for importing Russian crude oil
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Days after members of the U.S. Congress passed a new Russia sanctions law targeting India and other oil importers of Russian crude oil, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Sunday (September 27, 2026) met with a five-member Congressional Delegation headed by the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee chair Brian Mast.

The delegation included Bill co-sponsor Jimmy Patronis, Republican representative James Gallagher, and Democrat Hailey Stevens, both of whom voted in favour of it, as well as Shri Thanedar, an Indian-born U.S. lawmaker, who had voted against the Bill.

The meeting follows days after External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised India’s concerns about possible sanctions with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York, and Mr. Misri discussed the issue with U.S. Undersecretary of State for Political Affairs Allison Hooker.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctions against Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), passed in the U.S. Congress on September 16, mandates that U.S. President Donald Trump impose up to 100% sanctions on countries that buy Russian oil and extends sanctions on trade with Iran.
A determination on what kind of sanctions, if any, would be imposed on India is expected to be made next month, with a 30-day deadline pending.
Officials did not comment on whether Mr. Misri discussed or received any assurances on a waiver of the sanctions that can be granted under certain conditions.

“Discussions covered the entire gamut of India-U.S. relations, including the recently enacted SRIA legislation and the future trajectory of the relationship,” Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a post about the meeting that was held at Mr. Misri’s residence.
“They also exchanged views on international issues of mutual concern, energy security, counter-terrorism and freedom of navigation,” he added.
Also read: 100% U.S. tariff threat: Can India’s new trade deals reduce its dependence on America?
Mr. Mast is an American Army veteran who lost both his legs in a blast in Kandahar in 2010.
He works on counter-terrorism issues and has an interest in South Asia.

During the India-Pakistan conflict in May 2025, Mr. Mast said in an interview that he had spoken to “both sides” and urged de-escalation after India’s strikes on Pakistan following the Pahalgam terror attacks.

stories.headline: | Supreme Court Asks Centre To Explain Decision To Levy Charges On UPI Transactions, Refuses Stay
stories.title: BREAKING | Supreme Court Asks Centre To Explain Decision To Levy Charges On UPI Transactions, Refuses Stay
stories.summary: The Government of India is not taking a single rupee of the charges, the Centre told the Court.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Government of India is not taking a single rupee of the charges, the Centre told the Court.

The Supreme Court on Monday called for an affidavit from the Union Government explaining the basis for the move to levy charges for transactions through Unified Payment Interface (UPI) above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a writ petition filed by Advocate Anjan Datta challenging Gazette notifications issued by the Union Ministry of Finance on September 14 and 15, announcing charges on commercial UPI transactions above ₹2,000.
At the outset, Additional Solicitor General N Venkataraman, for the Union, submitted that the charges will take effect only on October 15.
He said that 96% of the transactions will not face the charge, and the charges for essential services have been capped as Rs 5.
"It is neither a tax nor a fee," ASG said.
"We need these facts on affidavit.
It's more of a technical issue," CJI Surya Kant said.
"Is it tax or a fee?
If not a fee, what is the executive basis for making this expropriation?
What is the service?" Justice Bagchi sought to know.

"It is not an expropriation," ASG affirmed, adding that the Government of India was not taking a single rupee out of the charges, and it was a settlement fee between the payment aggregators and the banks.

sentences.text: A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a writ petition filed by Advocate Anjan Datta challenging Gazette notifications issued by the Union Ministry of Finance on September 14 and 15, announcing charges on commercial UPI transactions above ₹2,000.

The Supreme Court on Monday called for an affidavit from the Union Government explaining the basis for the move to levy charges for transactions through Unified Payment Interface (UPI) above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants.
At the outset, Additional Solicitor General N Venkataraman, for the Union, submitted that the charges will take effect only on October 15.
He said that 96% of the transactions will not face the charge, and the charges for essential services have been capped as Rs 5.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday urged the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly to decide by October 8 the petitions filed by Trinamool Congress (Mamata Banerjee) member Sohandeb Chattopadhyay seeking the disqualification of ten MLAs of the Ritabrata Banerjee faction under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution for alleged defection.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana disposed of the writ petition filed by Sohandeb Chattopadhyay seeking expeditious decision by the Speaker.

Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal, for the petitioner, submitted that there was a pattern of delaying decisions on disqualification petitions, and the breakaway faction consequently getting a declaration that they were the real party.
The bench said that it will dispose of the petition urging the Speaker to follow the decision in Keisham Meghachandra Singh.
The Hon'ble Speaker Manipur Legislative Assembly and others which held that disqualification petitions must be decided within three months.
Noting that the disqualification petitions were filed on July 8, 2026, the Court expressed that the Speaker is expected to take a decision by October 8, 2026.
"This Court in Keshaj Meghamchandra Singh has authoritatively ruled that disqualification petitions are expected to be decided within a reasonable period, say three months.
The petitions were filed against Arup Roy, Ritabrata Banerjee, Firad Hakim, Sandipan Saha, Seuli Saha, Akrhruzzaman, Sabina Yeasmin, Rathin Ghosh, Biplab Mitra, and Javed Ahmad Khan.
Senior Advocate Kalyan Bandhopadhyay also appeared for the petitioner.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With just three days left in the south-west monsoon season, the Bay of Bengal has stirred into another bout of activity, with an incoming weather pulse from Thailand intensifying rapidly over the weekend into a depression by Monday morning.

The development had been flagged by businessline eight days ago, based on India Meteorological Department (IMD) numerical model guidance, which had indicated the potential for the system to emerge over the Bay and intensify.
The latest depression, however, is unlikely to turn towards the Indian coast.

The IMD said it could strengthen further into a deep depression by this (Monday) evening and move along and off the Myanmar coast towards north-east and adjoining Bangladesh coast over next three days.
The depression lay over the north Andaman Sea and adjoining Myanmar coast, about 590 km east-north-east of Mayabandar in the Andaman Islands.
The Bay system’s evolution comes as the south-west monsoon steadily retreats from the mainland, clearing the stage for seasonal transition to the north-east monsoon.

The withdrawal line on Monday passed through Gurdaspur; Chandigarh; Muzaffarnagar; Aligarh; Dholpur; Udaipur; Deesa; and Naliya, marking further retreat across Punjab; Chandigarh-Haryana-Delhi; Uttar Pradesh; Rajasthan; and Gujarat.
A residual low-pressure area over east Uttar Pradesh, remnant of the preceding deep depression, has weakened as withdrawal accelerated across northern India.
The transition is expected to become evident first over the Arabian Sea, where south-westerly winds ay give way to easterlies by around October 7.
The Bay could take slightly longer to fall into step, with short-to medium-range guidance pointing to a shift around October 12.
That change in wind regime could open the door to a fresh spell of rain and thunderstorms across larger Peninsular India and the South Peninsula, even as the south-west monsoon formally winds down.
The IMD outlook points to a broadening spell of rain and thunderstorms from the middle of the week.
